finding.text: There is no `requirements.md` at the top of this task folder (mastermind-session-truth/), only `brief-common.md` and one per sub-folder (`score-endings/requirements.md`, `truth/requirements.md`). I judged the diff against `score-endings/requirements.md`, the brief it matches. A fresh agent could not find the owner's ask for this change from the top folder, so link or copy it there.

The code change is small and correct. `core/Task/Task.js:390` now counts a turn Prompt marked `no_action` as finished, not open. `Prompt.js:128` already scores such a turn 1, so tally and score now agree. `Session.test.mjs:133` asserts `tally().open === 0`, and both `Session.test.mjs` and `completion.test.mjs` pass when I ran them.

`completion.test.mjs` has no check for the new `no_action` branch in `tally()`. The one assertion is in `Session.test.mjs` and goes through a replayed turn. Add a one-line check beside the other tally checks in `core/Task/completion.test.mjs`, since `tally()` is a Task method.

The `SessionFolders` readme line (`core/Session/readme.md:39`) now documents `.url(id)` and `url_in`. Both already exist at `SessionFolders.mjs:173` and `:179`, with callers such as `Servex/ext/refine/CardAsk.js:45`, so this is a catch-up and the line is accurate. `SessionFolders.test.mjs` exists, but I did not check whether it covers `url`/`url_in`.

`doc/completion.md` and the `core/Task/readme.md` "No silent endings" bullet now say the closing task is filed only when `SERVEX_OPEN_ITEMS=on`, and the dry-run link is fixed. They agree with each other. The timing range "0.4-1.2 s" replaces "0.5-0.7 s", which is fine as a re-measure, but no measuring command is cited.
The diff has no UI change, so there are no shots and no Words or layout questions to answer. The readme edits are plain and carry no dated logs.

The named brief `mastermind-session-truth/requirements.md` does not exist (the briefs sit one level down, e.g. `truth/requirements.md`), and the diff matches none of them: it is a small tally fix, not the truth page or the twin fold. A fresh agent cannot tell which ask this diff answers; add a requirements.md (or a task line) at the folder root that names it.

`core/Task/Task.js:390` counts a task with `no_action` as `finished` but never runs `Task.proof_problem` on it, and `core/Task/readme.md` (the `tally()` line, "counts created/finished/stopped/open") and `doc/completion.md` do not say that a `no_action` turn now lands in `finished`. Add one sentence to the readme's `tally()` description so the counts are explained where they are defined.

The code change is correct and tested: `completion.test.mjs` (new `s4c` case) and `Session.test.mjs:133` both assert `tally().open === 0` after `no_action`. It reads `k.no_action` as a plain field, which works because Item assigns unknown keys, but there is no declared getter in `Task.js`.

`Session/readme.md:39` now documents `url(id)` and `url_in(repo, id)`, which match `SessionFolders.mjs:173,179` and are tested at `SessionFolders.test.mjs:77-84`. The `completion.md` edits (switch-on wording, 0.4-1.2 s timing) are accurate and consistent with `Task/readme.md`.
The diff has no UI, so the `shots/` folder in the task folder is unrelated to it and nothing in `shots/` can show this change.

`requirements.md` does not list this diff's ask: the task is `t13-shell-commits` (session.jsonl:196, "from voice-app 2026-11-07"), but the "Added by the owner later" section names only the flat route, the children link and the caution. Add a line for it, so a fresh agent can tell which ask diff.patch answers.

Task `t13-shell-commits` is still open. session.jsonl has its `add` line (196) and the commit 7ef46691d (221), but no close with an outcome, and the branch `worktree/shell-commits` is not merged into compliance/dev. Close the task with its evidence (the two test runs below) and land the branch.

`Servex/ext/remote/doc/remote-tools.md:5` describes `shell` but does not say that a commit made through it now lands on the voice app's record of the day, through `SERVEX_SESSION_ID`/`SERVEX_SESSION_RECORD`. Add one sentence, linked to `Server/git-hooks/readme.md`. `Server/git-hooks/readme.md` is current.

The ask is met, and it is tested. In the worktree, `node Server/git-hooks/CommitLog.test.mjs` passes 10 checks: the shell caller's commit lands on its record with a `Session: cloud-voice-app-…` trailer, and a record whose line 1 names another id is never written. `RemoteMCP.test.mjs` passes, including the new `SERVEX_SESSION_ID` check.

`caller_session` arrives as an ordinary tool argument (`Servex/files.js:116`, `a.caller_session`). `RemoteMCP.intercept` (`RemoteMCP.js:188`) overwrites it only when a voice session exists, so any other caller can pass its own `{id, file}` and log a commit on any record whose line-1 id it knows. The line-1 check limits the damage. Passing the caller through `ctx` instead of the args would be simpler and could not be spoofed.

`env_of` deletes `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, and `shell_caller` returns null when a uuid `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is set. Each guard alone settles who owns the commit, and the comments in both files say why. That is consistent, not a bug. Only the remote door sets `caller_session`, so local agents' shell commits behave exactly as before.
No page changed, so this review has only the Requirements and Words checks. The `shots/` folder in this task folder belongs to earlier work and has nothing to do with this diff.

The ask (t13, requirements.md "Added 2026-11-07") is met and tested. In the worktree `C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/shell-commits` (head ee5bff40b), `node Server/git-hooks/CommitLog.test.mjs` passes 10 checks and `node Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.test.mjs` passes. The tests show a shell caller's commit landing on its record with a `Session: cloud-voice-app-…` trailer, and a record whose line 1 names another id never being written.

All three fixes from the first review are done. requirements.md now lists t13 and t14, `Servex/ext/remote/doc/remote-tools.md:6` describes commits made through `shell`, and the caller now travels in `ctx.session`, not in an argument. `RemoteMCP.intercept` (`RemoteMCP.js:193`) sets it under a Symbol key, so a JSON body cannot spoof it, and both dispatch paths pass it on (`RemoteMCP.js:137`, `:145`).

Task `t13-shell-commits` is still open in session.jsonl (only its `add` line, :196), and `worktree/shell-commits` is not merged yet. That is correct before a review passes. Once the branch lands, close t13 with the outcome and the two test runs as evidence.

The `RemoteMCP.test.mjs:113` check reads only `SERVEX_SESSION_ID`. A wrong `SERVEX_SESSION_RECORD` path (for example, if `voice_session`'s `file` ever stopped being relative to `public/`) would pass that check, and the hook would then fail quietly on line 1. One more line, asserting that the echoed record path exists, would close that gap.

The change is as simple as it can be. A simpler version would need the cloud id to be a uuid, which would rename every existing cloud record. Local agents' shell commits behave exactly as before, because `env_of` returns `process.env` unchanged when there is no `ctx.session` (`Servex/files.js:58`).

The new reader repeats an existing one (law 6, "one of everything"). `Server/RefineQueue.mjs:57` `RefineQueue.owner_text(line)` already turns one transcript line into the owner's words, and it filters more: it strips reminders through `RefinedCard.strip`, and it drops `[You are …` briefs, `[from: …` relays, `Caveat:` lines and "This session is being continued" summaries. `Server/ClaudeCodeTranscript.mjs:23` `is_owner` misses those, so on a local SDK agent's transcript the spawn brief counts as an owner turn. Make `ClaudeCodeTranscript` call one shared filter (move `owner_text` into it, or import it), so both readers agree.

The doc doesn't say how the new reader relates to the old ones. `Server/doc/transcripts.md` (new section "One transcript, the owner's turns") never mentions `RefineQueue.owner_text` or its doc `ext/Refine/doc/refine-queue.md`. Its numbering also differs: `#n` here is the owner-turn count, while RefineQueue's `<session>:<line>` is the transcript's line number. A reader can't move between the two without investigating. One sentence and a link would fix it.

A fresh agent can't pick up t14 from the task folder alone. `calibration/` has `instructions.md`, 4 inputs and 8 Haiku and Sonnet outputs, but no readme or status line. It doesn't say which steps are done (inputs and the two model runs) and which are left (the Opus judging, coverage against the 24 tasks of the voice-app record, the /live/ sub-page). The task line `t14-calibration` in `session.jsonl:435` points at `calibration/results.md`, which doesn't exist. `calibration/` is also untracked in git (`git status`: `??`), so none of this survives a lost working tree. Add a short `calibration/readme.md` that indexes the files and lists the next step, and commit it.

Requirements check for t14's "a transcript reader named for Claude Code transcripts": met. The test passes in the worktree (`node Server/ClaudeCodeTranscript.test.mjs`: PASS, 4 checks). The CLI run on `~/.claude/cloud-transcripts/cloud-8849dcc6.jsonl` gives 147 owner turns, and none starts with `<` or a harness note. The rest of t14 (Opus judge, coverage, /live/ suggestions page, staying within about $5) isn't in this diff, so it isn't judged here.

The commit `2b0ff8539` sits on `worktree/shell-commits`, the t13 branch that was already merged (`397c6d72d Merge shell-commits`). The brief names that branch for t13 only. A t14 branch would keep the landing log readable: this merge will read as "shell-commits" again.

`Server/readme.md:54` indexes the new tool, and its doc is linked. `ClaudeCodeTranscript.sentences` (`Server/ClaudeCodeTranscript.mjs:37`) splits "e.g. this" and "monorepo.lu42.com. There" at the same marks. That's fine for pointing at a sentence, but the calibration inputs number sentences with `[n]`, and they need to use this same split or the judge's coverage numbers won't line up.

Task t14 is never closed: `session.jsonl:435` adds `t14-calibration`, but no later line closes it with an outcome and evidence, and `requirements.md` still shows `- [ ] **t14, calibration:**` even though its own text says "Done". After the reader lands, close t14 with its proof (the merge, `calibration/results.md`, `/live/calibration/`) and tick the box.

All three fixes from the last review are in (commit 2a3d59f33). `RefineQueue.owner_text` now just calls `ClaudeCodeTranscript.owner_text` (`Server/RefineQueue.mjs:58`), so there is one filter. `Server/doc/transcripts.md` explains how it relates to RefineQueue and how the two number turns. `calibration/` now has a readme and results.md, and both are in git. In the worktree, `node Server/ClaudeCodeTranscript.test.mjs` passes 5 checks and `node Server/PromptAudit-stream.test.mjs` prints ok.

The shared filter now also drops `[Request interrupted…` lines (`Server/ClaudeCodeTranscript.mjs:25`). This changes RefineQueue and PromptAudit too, which will no longer file "[Request interrupted by user]" as an owner prompt. It's a good change, but the commit message doesn't mention it.

There is still a third owner-prompt filter: `Server/AskTally.mjs:45` has its own regex, with a slightly different list (`<`, `Base directory for this skill`). Law 6 says to point it at `ClaudeCodeTranscript.owner_text` in a later small step. That code isn't in this diff, so this is a note and not a fix.
Both t14 commits (2b0ff8539, 2a3d59f33) are still on `worktree/shell-commits`, the t13 branch that was already merged. The landing log will show this as "shell-commits" again.

`Server/readme.md:54` indexes the new tool and its test. `Server/doc/transcripts.md` documents it. `calibration/readme.md` links back to it. Nothing new is left unindexed, and a fresh agent could pick up t14 from `calibration/readme.md` alone.
